## Installation

```{r install, eval = FALSE}
install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("IMPALA-Consortium/gsm.ctas")
```

```{r load, message = FALSE}
library(gsm.ctas)
library(dplyr)
```

## The shape of the pipeline


## Input data

`gsm.ctas` ships verbatim copies of the SDTM domains needed by the workflow
(`dm`, `lb`, `vs`, `eg`, `rs`) alongside a synthetic `queries` frame matching
the ctasapp upload contract, so the walkthrough runs without any external
data dependency.

```{r data}

dfDM <- gsm.ctas::dm
dfVS <- gsm.ctas::vs
dfLB <- gsm.ctas::lb
dfRS <- gsm.ctas::rs
dfEG <- gsm.ctas::eg
dfQueries <- gsm.ctas::queries

lRaw <- list(
  Raw_DM = as.data.frame(dfDM),
  Raw_VS = as.data.frame(dfVS),
  Raw_LB = as.data.frame(dfLB),
  Raw_RS = as.data.frame(dfRS),
  Raw_EG = as.data.frame(dfEG),
  Raw_Queries = as.data.frame(dfQueries)
)
```

## 1. Mapping

```{r mappings}
lMappingWorkflows <- workr::MakeWorkflowList(
  strNames = NULL,
  strPath = system.file("workflow/1_mappings", package = "gsm.ctas"),
  strPackage = NULL
)

lIngest <- gsm.mapping::Ingest(
  lRaw, gsm.mapping::CombineSpecs(lMappingWorkflows)
)

lMapped <- suppressWarnings(
  gsm.core::RunWorkflows(lWorkflows = lMappingWorkflows, lData = lIngest)
)

str(lMapped)
```


## 2.1 Data Types / Metrics

`Standardize_Domain()` renames an SDTM domain into the CTAS vocabulary and,
by default, emits a numeric-ready frame that can flow straight into
`Analyze_CTAS()`. It also normalizes `visitnum` and `timepoint_rank` to a
contiguous `1..N` per `(subject_id, parameter_id)` -- matching ctasapp's
`recalculate_timepoint_rank()` convention -- so downstream shards read
cleanly regardless of how the source `VISITNUM` values were spaced.
Range, missing-ratio and categorical metrics chain an `Input_*()`
transform in between to overwrite `result` and `parameter_category_3`.

### Range-normalized labs

`Input_Range()` rescales each result into its reference range; values with
missing bounds are dropped.

```{r range}
as_tibble(lMapped$Mapped_LB)

dfStandard <- Standardize_Domain(
  dfDomain = lMapped$Mapped_LB,
  dfSubjects = lMapped$Mapped_Subjects,
  strTestCDCol = "LBTESTCD",
  strTestCol = "LBTEST",
  strValueCol = "LBSTRESN",
  strLowCol = "LBSTNRLO",
  strHighCol = "LBSTNRHI",
  strCategory = "Labs",
  strExcludePattern = NULL
)

as_tibble(dfStandard)

dfRange <- Input_Range(dfStandard)

as_tibble(dfRange)

dfAna <- Analyze_CTAS(dfRange)

as_tibble(dfAna)
```

### Numeric vital signs

`Standardize_Domain()` stamps `parameter_category_3 = "numeric"` and
`result = as.numeric(value)`, so no separate transform step is needed.

```{r numeric}
as_tibble(lMapped$Mapped_VS)

dfStandard <- Standardize_Domain(
  dfDomain = lMapped$Mapped_VS,
  dfSubjects = lMapped$Mapped_Subjects,
  strTestCDCol = "VSTESTCD",
  strTestCol = "VSTEST",
  strValueCol = "VSSTRESN",
  strCategory = "Vital Signs",
  strExcludePattern = NULL
)

as_tibble(dfStandard)

dfAna <- Analyze_CTAS(dfStandard)

as_tibble(dfAna)
```

### Ratio-missing labs

`Input_Missing()` converts each observation into a 0/1 indicator of whether
the value is missing, so the resulting CTAS signal is per-site missingness
over time.

```{r ratio_missing}
dfStandard <- Standardize_Domain(
  dfDomain = lMapped$Mapped_LB,
  dfSubjects = lMapped$Mapped_Subjects,
  strTestCDCol = "LBTESTCD",
  strTestCol = "LBTEST",
  strValueCol = "LBSTRESN",
  strCategory = "Labs",
  strExcludePattern = NULL
)

as_tibble(dfStandard)

dfMissing <- Input_Missing(dfStandard)

as_tibble(dfMissing)

dfAna <- Analyze_CTAS(dfMissing)

as_tibble(dfAna)
```

### Categorical response

`Input_OneHot()` expands a categorical variable such as SDTM RS `RSSTRESC`
into one binary CTAS timeseries per observed level, so `Analyze_CTAS()` can
flag sites whose per-level rates drift from their peers.

```{r categorical}
dfRS <- gsm.ctas::rs
dfRS <- dfRS[dfRS$RSTESTCD == "OVRLRESP", ]

dfStandard <- Standardize_Domain(
  dfDomain = dfRS,
  dfSubjects = lMapped$Mapped_Subjects,
  strTestCDCol = "RSTESTCD",
  strTestCol = "RSTEST",
  strValueCol = "RSSTRESC",
  strCategory = "Disease Response",
  strExcludePattern = NULL
)

as_tibble(dfStandard)

dfOneHot <- Input_OneHot(dfStandard)

as_tibble(dfOneHot)

unique(dfOneHot$parameter_id)

dfAna <- Analyze_CTAS(dfOneHot)

as_tibble(dfAna)
```

### Stitching metrics on the same field

ctasapp groups sidebar entries by `parameter_category_2`, so when the same
LB test flows through both `Input_Range()` and `Input_Missing()` the two
metrics collapse into a single field entry with a faceted plot.
`Standardize_Domain()` sets `parameter_category_2` to the raw test code
(e.g. `"ALT"`); the `Input_*()` wrappers only prefix `parameter_id` itself
(`RANGE_ALT`, `MISS_ALT`) so the score tables stay unique.

```{r stitching}
dfLB <- Standardize_Domain(
  dfDomain = lMapped$Mapped_LB,
  dfSubjects = lMapped$Mapped_Subjects,
  strTestCDCol = "LBTESTCD",
  strTestCol = "LBTEST",
  strValueCol = "LBSTRESN",
  strLowCol = "LBSTNRLO",
  strHighCol = "LBSTNRHI",
  strCategory = "Labs",
  strExcludePattern = NULL
)

intersect(
  unique(Input_Range(dfLB)$parameter_category_2),
  unique(Input_Missing(dfLB)$parameter_category_2)
) |> head()
```

### EDC queries

`Standardize_Queries()` mirrors `Standardize_Domain()` for EDC query records:
it translates the ctasapp query upload schema (`study`, `domain`, `field`,
`subject_id`, `visit`, `parameter_id`) into the CTAS long vocabulary and
inner-joins `Mapped_Subjects` on `(studyid, subject_id)`. `domain` becomes
`parameter_category_1` via a fixed map (`LB` -> `"Labs"`, `VS` ->
`"Vital Signs"`, `EG` -> `"ECG"`, `RS` -> `"Disease Response"`; unknown
values pass through verbatim), `field` becomes `parameter_category_2`, and
the original 15 upload columns are preserved for downstream joins.

```{r queries_standardize}
dfQ <- Standardize_Queries(
  dfQueries = lMapped$Mapped_Queries,
  dfSubjects = lMapped$Mapped_Subjects
)

as_tibble(dfQ)
```



## 2. Metrics

```{r metrics}
lMetricWorkflows <- workr::MakeWorkflowList(
  strNames = NULL,
  strPath = system.file("workflow/2_metrics", package = "gsm.ctas"),
  strPackage = NULL
)

lAnalysis <- suppressWarnings(
  gsm.core::RunWorkflows(lWorkflows = lMetricWorkflows, lData = lMapped)
)

str(lAnalysis)
```

Feature selection is one boolean per CTAS feature in `meta:`, so any metric
can toggle features individually:

```yaml
meta:
  ID: numeric
  FeatureAutocorr: true
  FeatureAverage: true
  FeatureSD: true
  FeatureRange: false
  FeatureUniqueValueCountRelative: true
  FeatureOwnSiteSimilScore: false
  FeatureLOF: false
```

Multi-study is honoured automatically: when `Mapped_Subjects` contains several
values in `studyid`, `Analyze_CTAS()` splits the input by study, runs CTAS on
each, and stacks the results with a `study` column tagged onto every row.

## 3. Reporting: writing ctasapp shards

`Bind_Analysis()` concatenates one named shard (`"results"`, `"input"` or
`"untransformed"`) across every metric workflow output; `Results.yaml`
wraps three of those steps into a single reporting call and packages the
three bound frames as a list ready to be handed to
[ctasapp](https://github.com/IMPALA-Consortium/ctasapp) validators or
written to parquet.

```{r reporting_results, eval = FALSE}
lReportingWorkflows <- workr::MakeWorkflowList(
  strNames = NULL,
  strPath = system.file("workflow/3_reporting", package = "gsm.ctas"),
  strPackage = NULL
)

lReporting <- gsm.core::RunWorkflows(
  lWorkflows = lReportingWorkflows,
  lData = c(lMapped, list(lAnalyzed = lAnalysis))
)

str(lReporting)
```

`Write_ctasapp()` walks the reporting output and writes every frame it
finds -- `results`, `input`, `untransformed` from the `Results` workflow
and `queries` from the `Queries` workflow -- as parquet (or csv) in one
call. Empty frames are skipped; a mis-shaped input errors rather than
producing an empty directory.

```{r reporting, eval = FALSE}
Write_ctasapp(lReporting, strDir = "pub", strFormat = "parquet")
```

Point [ctasapp](https://github.com/IMPALA-Consortium/ctasapp) at the same
`pub/` folder by copying the shipped `ctasapp.yml` next to `app.R` and
setting its `embedded:` block to the parquet files written above.
`run_ctas_app()` discovers the config in the current working directory and
loads the embedded dataset through the same validation pipeline it uses
for uploads.

```{r ctasapp, eval = FALSE}
# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("IMPALA-Consortium/ctasapp")

file.copy(
  system.file("ctasapp.yml", package = "ctasapp"),
  "ctasapp.yml",
  overwrite = TRUE
)

# Edit ctasapp.yml so the embedded block points at pub/:
#
# embedded:
#   results: pub/results.parquet
#   input: pub/input.parquet
#   untransformed: pub/untransformed.parquet  # optional

ctasapp::run_ctas_app()
```

## 4. Reporting: rendering the standard gsm KRI report

The `Summary.yaml` reporting workflow aggregates the long CTAS `results`
frame into the gsm reporting `dfResults` contract (one row per site x
synthetic `MetricID`), so the stock `gsm.kri` KRI report can render it
unchanged. Each `parameter_category_2` (data field, e.g. `"AST"`,
`"SYSBP"`) becomes its own `MetricID`; per-site `Score` is the maximum
`fdr_corrected_pvalue_logp` across every contributing (timeseries x
feature) row. Sites present in `Mapped_Subjects` but with no scored
timeseries stay in the frame with `Score = NA` so the KRI overview widget
cannot silently drop them.

### `Summarize_CTAS()` + `Flag_CTAS()` directly

`Summarize_CTAS()` and `Flag_CTAS()` mirror the `gsm.core::Summarize()` /
`gsm.core::Flag()` seam so thresholds can be retuned without
re-aggregating. `Flag_CTAS()` uses left-closed intervals appropriate for
the non-negative `-log10(p)` scale, with defaults `vThreshold = c(0.842,
2.326)` (80% and 99% one-sided normal z-quantiles) and three flag levels
(`0` green, `1` amber, `2` red).

```{r summarize_direct, eval = FALSE}
dfResultsLong <- lReporting$Reporting_Results$results

dfScores <- Summarize_CTAS(
  dfResults = dfResultsLong,
  dfSubjects = lMapped$Mapped_Subjects
)

as_tibble(dfScores)

dfFlagged <- Flag_CTAS(dfScores)

as_tibble(dfFlagged)
```

Pass `bByFeature = TRUE` to split one `MetricID` per (field x CTAS
feature) instead of collapsing to one `MetricID` per field, or
`bIncludeMissingness = FALSE` to drop the `ratio_missing` metric family
from the aggregation.

### Running the `Summary` workflow

`Summary.yaml` (Priority 3) chains `Summarize_CTAS()` -> `Flag_CTAS()` ->
`Make_KRI_Metrics()` -> `Make_KRI_Groups()` into a single reporting call
and packages the three frames the stock `gsm.kri` report needs. Every
threshold and grouping choice is a workflow `meta` parameter so a
sponsor can retune the report in YAML without editing R.

Fields that never triggered a flag are dropped after `Flag_CTAS()` by
`Filter_Flagged()` so the rendered report stays short. The cutoff is the
`iMinFlag` meta parameter (default `1`, i.e. keep any metric with at
least one amber or red site); set to `0` to keep every field, or `2` to
keep only fields with at least one red flag.

```yaml
meta:
  ID: Summary
  IncludeMissingness: true
  ByFeature: false
  vThreshold: [0.842, 2.326]
  vFlag: [0, 1, 2]
  vFlagOrder: [2, 1, 0]
  iMinFlag: 1
```

```{r summary_workflow, eval = FALSE}
lReportingWorkflows <- workr::MakeWorkflowList(
  strNames = NULL,
  strPath = system.file("workflow/3_reporting", package = "gsm.ctas"),
  strPackage = NULL
)

lReporting <- gsm.core::RunWorkflows(
  lWorkflows = lReportingWorkflows[c("Results", "Summary")],
  lData = c(lMapped, list(lAnalyzed = lAnalysis))
)

str(lReporting$Reporting_Summary, max.level = 1)
```

### Rendering the KRI HTML report

`report_kri_site.yaml` in `inst/workflow/4_modules/` calls
`gsm.kri::MakeCharts()` + `gsm.kri::Report_KRI()` on the packaged summary
and writes a site-level HTML report with the standard gsm KRI layout: a
site x metric icon overview and one bar chart per `MetricID`. The output
file name is auto-generated from `StudyID`, `GroupLevel` and
`SnapshotDate` (e.g. `kri_report_CDISCPILOT01_Site_20260831.html`); the
output directory defaults to the current working directory and can be
overridden by mutating the workflow object.

```{r report_kri, eval = FALSE}
lModuleWorkflows <- workr::MakeWorkflowList(
  strNames = NULL,
  strPath = system.file("workflow/4_modules", package = "gsm.ctas"),
  strPackage = NULL
)

# Optional: point the report at a specific directory (must already exist).
# dir.create("pub", showWarnings = FALSE)
# lModuleWorkflows$report_kri_site$meta$strOutputDir <- "pub"

gsm.core::RunWorkflows(
  lWorkflows = lModuleWorkflows,
  lData = lReporting
)
```
